strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation with principled approach to weather editing via intrinsic space decomposition, addressing fundamental limitations of pixel-space methods
Comprehensive technical framework combining inverse rendering, weather-aware diffusion with intrinsic map-aware attention (IMAA), and forward rendering with coherent design
Extensive experimental validation including quantitative metrics across multiple aspects, comparisons with diverse baselines, ablation studies, and user study with perceptual evaluation
Valuable dataset contribution (WeatherSynthetic 35K + WeatherReal 18K) with intrinsic map annotations fills gap for outdoor driving scene resources
Strong quantitative results demonstrating superiority in plausibility (CLIP-S), structure preservation (DINO-ST), and downstream task performance on ACDC benchmark
Convincing visual quality in comparisons showing superior control and geometric/material preservation with minimal distortion or hallucination compared to pixel-space methods
Thorough supplementary material with additional ablations, comparisons, and failure case analysis demonstrating research thoroughness
weaknesses: Temporal consistency explicitly unsupported for video sequences—critical limitation for autonomous driving applications where the method is motivated, acknowledged but left as future work

Inverse rendering accuracy issues: estimated maps contain errors (shown in Fig 9) that propagate to final results; no error propagation analysis, uncertainty quantification, or failure handling strategies
Severe domain limitation: all experiments on outdoor driving scenes only; generalization to indoor/other domains unclear; design specifically tailored to this narrow use case
Computational efficiency completely unaddressed: no inference time comparisons, training cost analysis, or scalability discussion despite practical deployment importance
Hyperparameter choices lack principled justification: IMAA loss weights (λ₁=1.0, λ₂=0.5, λ₃=0.1) and distillation parameters appear arbitrary without sensitivity analysis
Insufficient analysis of failure modes: method fails on dense fog (Fig 25) with acknowledged statement that 'background details are unreliable' but no mitigation strategies proposed

Evaluation rigor gaps: user study lacks statistical significance testing/confidence intervals, some baselines not specifically designed for weather editing, missing comparisons with recent diffusion weather methods
Inverse rendering quality-to-synthesis performance relationship not rigorously analyzed; how imperfect maps affect final quality unclear despite acknowledged inaccuracies
Dataset annotation quality undocumented: no inter-annotator agreement, validation procedures, or discussion of pseudo-label reliability for WeatherReal
Limited technical novelty in components: inverse renderer based on prior VAE work, forward renderer uses standard CLIP interpolation; main novelty is their combination with IMAA

strengths: Novel and well-motivated intrinsic-space formulation that directly addresses limitations of pixel-space weather editing for preserving geometry and materials
Technical soundness of the two-component inverse/forward rendering architecture with clear practical advantages demonstrated in qualitative comparisons
Intrinsic Map-Aware Attention (IMAA) is a clever contribution that effectively addresses outdoor scene challenges; ablations confirm ~1.2 dB improvement on albedo PSNR
Strong empirical results: ~10 dB PSNR improvement in inverse rendering over prior methods (27.99 vs 11.91 for DiffusionRenderer on albedo)

Comprehensive experimental validation including quantitative comparisons across multiple method categories, user study (81.67% preference), and substantial downstream improvements on ACDC (87.1% AP75 gain, 24.5% mIOU gain)
Valuable dataset contribution addressing gap in large-scale outdoor weather-diverse autonomous driving datasets with intrinsic map annotations
Clear presentation with effective visualizations demonstrating preservation of scene structure while modifying weather
weaknesses: Temporal inconsistency in video sequences (Fig. 12) is acknowledged but not addressed; this is a significant practical limitation for autonomous driving applications where temporal coherence is essential

Limited real-world evaluation and validation: WeatherReal pseudo-labels generated using the inverse renderer create circular dependency; most quantitative results emphasize synthetic WeatherSynthetic; generalization to unseen real-world conditions not systematically evaluated

Evaluation relies on proxy metrics (CLIP-S, DINO-S, PSNR/SSIM) that measure text-image consistency and structure rather than physical plausibility or correctness; no ground-truth intrinsic map comparison demonstrating physical validity
Questionable core assumption that albedo/roughness/metallicity are weather-invariant—wet surfaces have different reflectance properties; no validation that PBR model holds for real outdoor scenes

Technical justifications incomplete: CLIP space interpolation assumes linearity (Eq. 2) is unvalidated; heuristic-guided IMAA training strategy relegated to supplementary without clear justification; feature distillation details absent, limiting reproducibility

Dataset construction concerns: WeatherReal uses Flux-Kontext to synthesize weather (introducing potential domain shift); pseudo-label quality validated only through manual spot-checking without systematic assessment

Incomplete ablation studies: no ablation on feature distillation component, CLIP interpolation strategy, or alpha sensitivity; limited analysis of when decomposition fails or how to handle weather types absent from training
Computational cost not addressed: no inference time, memory usage, or efficiency comparison—important for autonomous driving deployment
Limited real-world baseline comparisons: WeatherWeaver is essentially the only weather-specific baseline; most comparisons against general pixel-space editors not designed for weather
Irradiance map validation absent: no quantitative assessment of whether estimated illumination captures true scene lighting or shadow accuracy across weather conditions
